newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Italy, Spain can meet EMU targets - Matutes.
newsitem.headline: Italy, Spain can meet EMU targets - Matutes.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Tuesday Italy is capable of meeting the entry requirements for joining a European single currency.
He also told a news conference that there was "every probability" of Spain joining the single currency, the euro, from its planned start in 1999.
"Italy has shown its willingness to make the necessary adjustments to meet the (Maastricht) criteria," he said. "I think that for the time being it will be capable of doing so," he added.
He also said: "Spain has every probability of joining the first stage of Economic and Monetary Union."
"This government is firmly committed to meeting Maastricht criteria, which are the only conditions that will determine which countries will join this union in its first stage and which will not."
Matutes was responding to concerns in financial markets that so-called "Club Med" countries, including Italy, Spain and Portugal, may not qualify to join the euro in 1999.
"I think it is good if a large number of countries meet the (EMU) conditions," Matutes said.
